about: Bonvoyage protocol v1 test vectors. All binary values are base64url without padding. See README.md.

base64url.note: AR decodes to the same byte as AQ, and AQJ to the same bytes as AQI, but with non-zero unused bits.

hosts.note: localhost (with a port) is only a host in a client's development mode, which is off by default.

addresses.note: What a client may connect to after resolving a relay's name (section 1.2).
addresses.teredo_note: The last address is Teredo; the IPv4 address inside it is 192.168.1.1, stored with its bits inverted.

proof_of_work.note: `nonce` is the smallest one for 12 bits; any nonce whose digest starts with at least `bits` zero bits is valid.

must_accept.note: Each opens and passes steps 1 to 6 of receiving at time `now`.

may_reject.note: The spec lets a receiver accept or reject these (section 1.2). Either is conformant.

contact_checks.note: The recipient has ONE contact: created from `cards.valid` at time `contact.issued`, in state open. Handle the steps in order at time `now`. `expect` is what happens to the message: `discard`, `hold` (a valid ticket queued for a contact that is not confirmed), or `print`. A step with `action` instead of `sealed` is something the owner does. `state_after` and `pinned_after` describe the contact after the step.

steps.why: a valid message from a stranger: the pairing secret matches no contact
right pairing secret, but not a ticket: it does not pair, and nothing about it is recorded
right pairing secret, but the ticket is invalid: it does not pair either
right pairing secret and a valid ticket: the key is pinned, the owner is told, the ticket is held
same signing key and id as the previous message: a repeat
right pairing secret and a valid ticket, but the contact is pinned to another key: a second party has the card
a second ticket from the pinned key, still not confirmed: held
the owner confirms: the contact is paired and its held tickets are printed
the pinned sender: the pairing secret is no longer looked at
authentic, but an unknown message type is dropped without printing (and recorded as handled)
created more than 600 seconds before the contact's card was issued
created exactly 600 seconds before the card was issued: still accepted

held_limit.note: A fresh copy of the same open contact. The first message pairs it (pending); of the next six tickets from that key, four more are held (five in total) and two are discarded.

expired_card.note: A fresh, open copy of the same contact, handled at time `now`, which is after the card expired.

two_contacts.note: The recipient has TWO open contacts: `first` with the pairing secret of `cards.valid`, and `second` with `second_pairing_secret`. This recipient confirms automatically, so a pairing goes straight to paired. Each step says which contact the message belongs to.

steps.why: Kaj pairs with the first contact
Kaj, already pinned, presents the second contact's secret: still the first contact, and the second stays open
Eve pairs with the second contact, with an id Kaj already used: handled messages are remembered per signing key
the same message from Eve again: a repeat

text_cleaning.note: C1 controls, DEL, carriage return, paragraph separator, BOM, a format character outside the basic plane
the joiners U+200D and U+200C are kept

relay_response.note: A collect response a client must handle: it looks at the first 20 entries only, and of those skips every one without a valid relay message id.
